The red velocity curve is almost horizontal before the collision, at about +3 m/s; then it bends downward and drops rapidly, crossing v=0 near the vertical grid line t=5 in the graph; afterward it continues to drop and gradually becomes flat, finally approaching -2 m/s. Reasoning: The question asks for the time when the magnitude of acceleration is the greatest. In a velocity-time graph, acceleration equals the slope dv/dt, so the position where the magnitude of acceleration is greatest is where the absolute value of the slope of the velocity curve is greatest. The steepest position of the red curve on the graph is in the middle of the descending process, about t=5. The horizontal-axis unit is marked as t (×10^-3) s, so this time is 5 × 10^-3 s.

method.method_draft: Inspect the velocity-time graph first: the red velocity curve is nearly horizontal at about +3 m/s before the collision, then drops most sharply near the middle of the transition, crosses v = 0 at the vertical grid line labeled t = 5, and becomes nearly horizontal again near -2 m/s. Use the text only to confirm this is a velocity-time graph for the billiard ball and that the question asks for the time when the magnitude of acceleration is greatest. Apply the rule that acceleration is the slope dv/dt of a velocity-time graph, so the magnitude of acceleration is greatest where the graph has the steepest slope in absolute value. The steepest part is at about t = 5 on the graph’s time axis. Since the axis is labeled t (×10^-3) s, report t = 5 × 10^-3 s.
